output.brief: Don't roll back the gateway. The evidence points to the storage compaction tuning change pushed on the evening of 2 Nov. Compaction worker threads went from 2 to 6 and took disk use from 41% to 97% within five minutes of the push in each cell. Disk read waits rose from 9 ms to 205 ms, and node-side GET time rose from 61 ms to 262 ms. In every cell, p99 jumped within minutes of that push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. For example, eu-w cells were still on 5.7 when they degraded. One cell, aps-3, skipped the push and stayed at about 94 ms even though it runs 5.8. A test rollback of eu-w-1 to 5.7 changed nothing. The network and traffic growth don't explain it. A rollback would also reopen the security hole with no latency benefit. Pausing compaction would risk disk-full and a backlog blow-up. Next step: revert the tuning in one cell and watch GET p99 and backlog, then extend it to the rest if it works. Treat the backlog as needing a durable, smaller compaction fix. Wait for the 10 Nov attribution before pacing Orrin. The projection shows no 15% breach before 13 Nov. Confidence is high.
